findings.title: Persist a prefix-causality regression that invokes the actual allocator
findings.evidence: The stored prefix test supplies a simple close-derived lambda rather than module_a_target. The allocation convention test at lines 143-148 covers a capped-weight hand case, zero/missing volatility and one-asset allocation, but not the multi-asset allocator's prefix invariance. The frozen original tests exercised the actual allocator at the cutoff; that exact coverage was not ported into the candidate test suite.
findings.impact: The stored candidate prefix test can remain green after a future look-ahead regression inside module_a_target or trailing_vol. This is a regression-coverage gap, not a demonstrated current allocator leak.
findings.verification: An independent in-memory probe in this review exercised module_a_target on four synthetic assets, preserved NAV and decisions through cutoff day 12 after future opens/closes were changed, and detected a deliberately next-day allocator at the cutoff. Current behavior passed, but this probe is not a persistent repository test.
findings.recommendation: In a later source-change cycle, persist the actual-allocator prefix probe with its next-day canary. No source or tests were changed in this GATE review.

shown_contracts.claim: The preserved original counterexample loses half the account when the sale-day future close is missing; the candidate sale and trace are unchanged by that missing unheld close.
Missing required execution opens refuse before that day's execution; missing held closes refuse after opening execution and retain cash/units. No undated recovery argument is accepted.

The candidate reconstructs sells-first cash credits/debits using multiplicative per-side fee and slippage, rejects material unaffordability or cash mismatch, and labels trace rows MODELLED. Numerical reconciliation allows the explicit scale-relative tolerance; it is not exact-decimal settlement proof.

Candidate/helper state parity passed at fee/slippage pairs (0,0), (0.005,0.0005) and (0.012,0.0005). Since parity uses the same shared helper, it is not an independent oracle by itself. Independent cash reconstruction, hand-calculated round trips and corruption canaries supply additional cost evidence.
